text:
jordan: FYI I'm hitting a subtle perf regression after we switched the rw-squad model to AWQ weight-only INT8 yesterday. P50 token latency up ~8% at steady state :thinking_face:
cheng: that sounds small but could be meaningful at scale. any profiler traces?
jordan: yes — ran the per-request flame with our perfkit. Most of the extra time is in the matmul kernel path and in the 'pack_weights' step. Also seeing slightly higher KV cache miss ratio in traces when group_size=64.
ben: @jordan can you paste the perf counters output? interested in kernel selection counts (fp8/int8/float fallback) and batching stats.
jordan: here's a cropped excerpt:

perf_counters: total_tokens=1_200_000
kernel_calls: int8_matmul=18_400, fp16_matmul=1_200, fallback_fp32=24
pack_time_ms=42.3, unpack_time_ms=1.8
kv_cache_hits=87.1%, kv_cache_misses=12.9%
batch_size_p95=6, continuous_batching_wait_ms=1.2

cheng: interesting that pack_time is 42ms — that's heavy. pack_time includes the AWQ group reordering + quant table lookup?
jordan: yes, current path does group-unpack -> reorder -> pack into blocking layout that our INT8 kernel prefers. For group_size=64 the loop is less cache-friendly on A100 due to the packing stride.
alicia: could also be due to kernel selection: if routing logic picks an int8 kernel that requires packed weights, we pay the pack cost once per model load, but our code currently packs lazily per request if model wasn't pinned. any chance of race with cold starts?
jordan: these are steady-state warm servers. Pack is happening per model-shard load when first batch processes — but some shards are being evicted more frequently due to KV cache pressure (we're storing larger KV for longer sequences). so pack time shows up during normal requests occasionally.
ben: two hypotheses: (1) group_size 64 increases per-shard memory so eviction rate up -> more packs; (2) the int8 kernel variant chosen is worse for our sequence length distribution. can we test group_size=32 and prepack at startup?
cheng: +1 for startup prepack. we also need to measure 'pack vs compute' ratio: an AWQ matmul should be much faster than fp16, but if pack is 40ms and compute is 30ms we lose.
perfbot: automated-bench: queued run 1759823501 for branch awq-int8/prepack-startup -> will run microbench: throughput/cold-start/steady for group_size 32/64/128. expected finish in ~6m.
jordan: added a quick microbench script I used:

```bash
# run inside runtime-container
python -m perfbench --model rw-squad-awq --group-size 64 --prepack false --seq-len 512 --threads 4 --duration 60
```

output snippet:
```
throughput_tokens_per_s: 1_850_000
avg_pack_time_ms: 42.3
avg_kernel_time_ms: 28.9
end_to_end_p50_ms_per_token: 0.78
```

alicia: if kernel_time is 28.9 and pack 42.3 then pack dominates. we should avoid per-request packing. two options: prepack at startup or change kernel to one accepting unpacked (slower compute but no pack). tradeoff: compute-only int8 kernel is ~40% slower than packed int8 on A100 but avoids pack cost.
ben: for group_size=32, what are the numbers?
jordan: microbench returns: group_size=32 -> pack_time_ms=22.1, kernel_time_ms=31.5, throughput_tokens_per_s: 1_960_000. kv_cache_misses drop to 9.8% in the trace because memory footprint smaller so fewer evictions.
cheng: so 32 looks like a sweet spot. less pack overhead, slightly higher kernel time but net positive. we should also check batching heuristic: current continuous_batching_wait_ms=1.2 which favors small batches. pushing that to 2.5ms might increase batch p95 and improve kernel utilization.
alicia: agree but need to be careful with latency SLOs. perhaps an adaptive policy that increases wait_ms when model variant is int8-packed and prepack not possible.
ben: next steps:
- run perfbot microbench for group_size 16/32/64 with and without prepack (I can parametrize)
- add a short-running experiment on staging with prepack at startup (pin shards)
- instrument kernel-selection logs to include selected variant and reason (e.g., memory, seq_len, quantization)
- add a counter for 'pack_done_per_shard' to measure how often pack happens in steady-state

jordan: i've opened a PR draft with a prepack flag and added pack_done_per_shard counters: https://git.redwood.example/rw/runtime/pull/421 (internal). notes in PR: prepack increases cold-start by ~12s but reduces steady p50 by ~7%.
perfbot: microbench results completed for awq-int8/prepack-startup (run 1759823501):
- group 16: throughput 2.05M t/s, avg_pack 12.2ms, kernel 33.1ms
- group 32: throughput 1.96M t/s, avg_pack 22.1ms, kernel 31.5ms
- group 64: throughput 1.85M t/s, avg_pack 42.3ms, kernel 28.9ms

cheng: looks consistent. we should also test kernel fallback logic: if int8 kernel fails (e.g., for seq_len > 1024), we fallback to fp16 and fallback path adds ~9ms due to copy and dtype conversion. are those cases common? j: occasional for long chats. but we can route long seqs to fp16 model variant.
alicia: one more thing — calibration: AWQ's per-group scale calibration can change compute patterns. did we use symmetric or asymmetric quant? jordan: symmetric. I suspect asymmetric might reduce pack complexity slightly because tables are smaller? need to check AWQ impl details.
ben: summary action items and owners:
- ben: run expanded microbench across instance types (A100, H100) and record kernel perf deltas.
- cheng: add kernel-selection reason field + bump batch wait adaptive heuristic prototype.
- jordan: merge prepack feature behind flag and run canary on staging pinned nodes. add pack_done_per_shard metrics to dashboards.
- alicia: coordinate with model-onboarding to test asymmetric calibration variant for AWQ and compare quality/loss/regression.

jordan: will run a 24h staging run and post perf dashboards tomorrow. tagging infra-bot to schedule a canary for 10 pinned shards at 3am UTC if everything looks ok.
infra-bot: scheduled canary awq-prepack-1759823610 -> start 1759862400, 10 pinned shards, rollback on p50 increase >3% or error rate >0.1%.
ben: perfect. thanks all. I'll follow up with the A100/H100 numbers in this thread when done. :thumbsup:
cheng: thanks — this feels actionable. if prepack + group=32 + small batch wait tweak yields consistent wins we can default to that for rw-squad and similar models.
alicia: also add a note in docs about tradeoffs so SREs know cold-start vs steady tradeoff.
perfbot: closing run summary for 1759823501.
